subject.title: fix: antml:/mm: namespaced tool-call XML leaks into chat replies (#97750)

question: May the shared sanitizer globally delete every full-line bare `<invoke>` block, even when the content is an unfenced user-authored XML example?
rationale: The proposed code cannot reliably distinguish a bare degraded proxy artifact from legitimate plain-text documentation, so choosing between leak suppression and content preservation is a product compatibility policy rather than a mechanical correctness decision.

options.title: Preserve ambiguous bare blocks
options.body: Restrict automatic stripping to namespaced forms or stronger tool-call context, keeping bare unwrapped XML visible unless a future owner-defined discriminator is available.

options.title: Accept global bare stripping
options.body: Keep the current behavior and explicitly document that all full-line bare invoke markup is treated as unsafe leaked tool-call text.

recommendation.title: Preserve ambiguous bare blocks
recommendation.body: Restrict automatic stripping to namespaced forms or stronger tool-call context, keeping bare unwrapped XML visible unless a future owner-defined discriminator is available.

likelyOwner.reason: Their adjacent namespaced streamed-text sanitizer work makes them the best available routing contact for the shared text-sanitization boundary.
